slides.text: AI Updates OpenAI GPT‑5.6 models: Sol, Terra, Luna GPT-5.6 Benchmarks https://openai.com/index/previewing-gpt-5-6-sol/ Sol - the flagship, highest‑capability (reasoning, complex coding, long‑horizon agentic tasks) Terra - balanced, similar to GPT 5.5 Luna - fastest and most affordable 1.5M-token context window Claude Sonnet 5 Not as good as Opus (but close) Lower cost -  $2/$10 in July-August after that 43 / $15 (compare - $5 / $25 for Opus 4.8) But it is actually more expensive than Opus because of updated tokenizer and high output token usage for reasoning tasks 1M context window https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-sonnet-5 https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing Claude Fable 5 is returning The US Department of Commerce has lifted the export controls on Claude Fable 5 and restored access on July 1st Safeguards were made stronger using "classifiers" Claude Fable 5 promotion July 1-7 Pro, Max, Team, and some Enterprise users could access it at no extra cost within their weekly usage limits (only up to 50% of your limits) Outside these promos, Fable 5 pricing is $10/$50 in/out per 1Mtok

slides.text: AI Updates Hermes MoA - Mixture-of-Agents https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mixture-of-agents https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent - 204K stars Each MoA “preset” defines one or more reference models plus an aggregator model The references run first, producing analysis that is passed as private context to the aggregator, which then generates the actual reply and tool calls You select MoA presets like any other model (via `/model`, `/moa`, CLI, dashboard, or desktop app), so they integrate seamlessly with goals, gateway sessions, and profiles Benchmarks show well-designed MoA presets can outperform any (single component) model on harder tasks On Hostinger, “Hermes Agent” is a one‑click Docker/VPS application for self‑hosting Nous Research’s Hermes agent, with optional bundled AI and scraping credits https://www.hostinger.com/applications/hermes-agent/1

slides.title: AI Updates We see a massive shift from
slides.text: AI Updates We see a massive shift from democratized AI to a highly regulated, government-approved ecosystem The U.S. government is now gating access to frontier models like GPT-5.6, creating a widening capability gap between internal lab technology and public tools Driven by extreme API costs, enterprises are shifting to cheaper Chinese open-source models like DeepSeek and GLM To protect profit margins and national security, closed U.S. labs are lobbying for regulations that could stifle open source Furthermore, the U.S. may label foreign models as "radioactive" security risks due to uninspectable "sleeper circuits," rendering them commercially unusable This fracturing environment risks crippling startups, driving tech founders out of America, and dividing the industry into a two-tier system controlled by elite institutions. Dark Ages Two classes: 1. Government and Big Companies - get best models first 2. Others - receive models later (if ever) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CTKe2tmdy7s

slides.title: AI Updates OpenAI "Jalapeno" AI chip for LLM
slides.text: AI Updates OpenAI "Jalapeno" AI chip for LLM Inference with Broadcom, initial deployment in late 2026 https://openai.com/index/openai-broadcom-jalapeno-inference-chip/ Google Gemini‑SQL2 A text‑to‑SQL system built on Gemini 3.1 Pro Translates natural‑language questions into executable, schema‑aware SQL queries for relational databases Gemini‑SQL2 uses multi‑step reasoning over database schemas and iterative candidate generation and verification, focusing on execution correctness rather than just syntactic validity On the BIRD benchmark, which stresses cross‑domain, noisy, and knowledge‑intensive text‑to‑SQL tasks, it achieves 80.04% execution accuracy, currently topping the single‑model leaderboard

slides.title: Ornith‑1.0 coding models Ornith‑1.0 coding models with their
slides.text: Ornith‑1.0 coding models Ornith‑1.0 coding models with their own harness Ornith is an open-source family of agentic coding models trained with RL to co-learn both task scaffolds (“harnesses”) and code solutions At the core of Ornith-1.0 is a self-improving training framework that jointly learns to solve tasks and to construct the scaffolds that guide those solutions Rather than relying on a fixed, human-designed harness shared across a task category, Ornith-1.0 treats the scaffold as a learnable object that co-evolves with the policy. You still run Ornith inside some outer environment, but much of the traditional, bespoke agent wiring is effectively absorbed into the model’s weights https://huggingface.co/collections/deepreinforce-ai/ornith-10 Ornith-1.0 ships in 9B, 31B, 35B-MoE, and 397B-MoE sizes under MIT, built on Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 ollama run hf.co/deepreinforce-ai/Ornith-1.0-9B-GGUF https://deep-reinforce.com/ornith_1_0.html https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDzw3qzmtvo DeepReinforce is a privately held, early-stage startup founded around 2024, 4 founders, Santa Clara, CA Led by Jiwei Li; few dozen employees; ~$100M in funding Note: DeepReinforce’s flagship product is IterX code optimization platform that combines LLM reasoning with reinforcement-learning style search over code edits Jiwei Li https://www.linkedin.com/in/jiwei-li-5293202a3/ “The name comes from the ancient Greek word for bird.”

slides.title: DeepSeek's DSpark DeepSeek's DSpark Open-source tool, accelerates LLMs
slides.text: DeepSeek's DSpark DeepSeek's DSpark Open-source tool, accelerates LLMs by 50% to 400% Uses speculative decoding , where a small, fast draft model predicts a block of tokens all at once, and a larger target model verifies them in a single pass DSpark improves on older methods by adding a lightweight serial head to prevent "suffix decay," ensuring guessed tokens connect logically to increase acceptance rates It also uses a confidence head to skip verifying low-probability tokens when servers are heavily loaded Already used in production for DeepSeek-V4, it delivers tokens up to 85% faster and can be attached to other open-source models like Qwen and Gemma https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSpec https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSpec/blob/main/DSpark_paper.pdf https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark

slides.title: Google Open Knowledge Format - OKF Google’s Open
slides.text: Google Open Knowledge Format - OKF Google’s Open Knowledge Format (OKF) A directory hierarchy of Markdown files with YAML front‑matter, designed so AI agents can read and reason over it directly https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/how-the-open-knowledge-format-can-improve-data-sharing Each OKF file has structure similar to skills - YAML front‑matter at the top followed by a Markdown body https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md Example (simplified): --- type: Playbook title: Refund Policy description: How we handle customer refund requests. tags: [support, policy] timestamp: 2026-06-01T10:00:00Z resource: https://internal.example.com/docs/refunds --- # Refund Policy We refund any order within 30 days of purchase… ----------------------------- Google’s Knowledge Catalog tools ingest OKF bundles and expose them as a searchable catalog, but the format itself is platform‑agnostic: you can store the files in Git, object storage, or any filesystem

slides.title: AI Updates "Six Power Phrases" for Claude Code
slides.text: AI Updates "Six Power Phrases" for Claude Code - by Austin Marchese 1. "Launch sub agents" 2. "Write me an implementation spec" 3. "Interview me" 4. "Verify before you build" 5. "Based on this conversation, build me a skill" 6. "Automate this" The most common mistake is failing to provide enough context or failing to create a plan https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TP73qyFWDcY Austin Marchese Ponytail prevents "verbose" behavior Opus 4.8 gets 71% faster, 71% fewer lines of code, and a 53% reduction in costs Ponytail is open-source (MIT), low-risk, recommended It is a plugin for AI coding agents. It provides rules (a strict decision ladder, “lazy senior dev” mode) so the agent writes only necessary code, avoiding verbose, over‑engineered outputs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aTPTUYC44ds https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail Google Pomelli - AI marketing agent Helps small and medium‑sized businesses create brand content It analyzes your website or uploaded materials to build a “Business DNA” profile capturing tone, colors, fonts, and imagery style Then Pomelli generates campaign ideas, social posts, ads, and simple websites, plus a brand book with consistent visual guidelines https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-labs/pomelli-agentic-capabilities/

slides.title: LangChain Is Dying LangChain Is Dying https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DnS-lA7SC0M Current
slides.text: LangChain Is Dying LangChain Is Dying https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DnS-lA7SC0M Current shift from heavy AI agent frameworks like LangChain to a lightweight "micro-agent" architecture Heavy frameworks introduce complex abstractions, increase token costs, and obscure prompts, making debugging exceptionally difficult In contrast, micro-agents function like microservices: they are small, single-purpose, and operate on a simple model, few tools, and a tight loop Emerging minimalist tools like Pydantic AI and Hugging Face's Small Agents provide type safety and direct Python execution While large frameworks remain useful for highly complex enterprise state management, the current movement emphasizes owning your prompts and context window The core takeaway is to always use the smallest, simplest tool that successfully completes the job "What you got was an agent inside an executor inside a chain your real prompt buried eight layers down under code you never wrote So developers are walking away... the abstractions are over-complicated, the docs never match. " "The bug isn't in your 50 lines, it's somewhere in the framework's 50,000 so you end up stepping through abstractions you didn't write in a stack trace that's mostly somebody else's code And the ground keeps moving under you. LangChain rocketed past a 100,000 GitHub stars and became just as famous for breaking changes between versions The interface you learned last quarter is deprecated... popularity was never the same thing as stability. "

slides.title: AI Updates LangChain Deep Agents Open-source (MIT) agent
slides.text: AI Updates LangChain Deep Agents Open-source (MIT) agent harness Includes plumbing like file systems, context management, sub-agents, planning, human gating, and tools Developers start with a complete, functioning terminal agent and trim away what they don't need Built on LangGraph, Deep Agents code is model-agnostic. It can be pointed at frontier APIs, open-weight cloud models, or fully local models via Ollama While Claude Code offers tighter integration and polish for Claude, Deep Agents provides the ultimate flexibility and sandboxing necessary for custom, multi-user AI engineering. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x6WyeI5yO9E Manolo Remiddi tests models for deep thinking GLM 5.2 wins,  Qwen3.6-27B is close second GPT-5.5 performed poorly because it was too agreeable https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zfgl5rA6ehg

slides.text: AI Updates Qwable 3.6 27B - by Mia-AiLab A fine-tuned version of the Qwen 3.6 27B For assistant-style and reasoning-heavy use cases Focuses on step-by-step responses Dario needs to be stopped Mehul Mohan critiques Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s 2023 testimony on open-weight AI risks Dario was saying that centralized models allow control and monitoring and proposes restricting open models Dario has claiming that open AI will enable catastrophic biological or cyber threats Mohan provides multiple reasons against Dario's position. He also talks about positive sides of open source (example - Linux). He explains that open-weight models, while not fully open source, still allow meaningful modification. Finally, he argues that restricting US AI development could weaken competitiveness, as global players continue advancing open-weight innovation. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EyARxk6y1_c X (formerly Twitter) MCP server to make its X easier to plug into AI tools and agents https://docs.x.com/tools/mcp https://mcp.directory/servers/x-twitter https://github.com/xdevplatform/xmcp Software is free, but access to Twitter data is not free

slides.title: AI Updates Become more effective with Claude Code
slides.text: AI Updates Become more effective with Claude Code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CBcyKfpldTo Create a " Brand Context Folder " as a permanent source of truth Voice Profile - defines your core voice rules and style Visual Identity - json or markdown file containing design tokens (fonts, colors, assets) Positioning - defines target audience, business goals, pain points. Use a "claude.md" file as an index that points to these context folders, preventing "context rot" by keeping individual files lean Autonomous Loops - keep running even without active supervision Auto Mode - use `Shift+Tab` twice to minimize interruptions, allowing Claude to perform safe actions automatically; "/goal" - set specific, measurable exit criteria so Claude knows exactly when a task is finished rather than completing it prematurely Loop/Routines - use to schedule recurring tasks (e.g., daily email/invoice processing) so the system works even when you are away from your computer. Handling Complex Tasks without losing focus or finishing prematurely Increase the "effort of thinking" (reasoning tokens);allow Claude to spin up a "team" of specialized agents, each with its own clean context, to tackle specific parts of a large project. Human-in-the-Loop - maintain intentional human checkpoints; identify the high-stakes points in your workflow where quality is critical; instruct Claude to pause at these stages, notify you, and wait for your review/edit before proceeding to production Goal - use AI for the repetitive 80% of research and drafting, while reserving your time for the 20% that provides human value.

slides.title: Pulumi vs Terraform Pulumi and Terraform - Infrastructure
slides.text: Pulumi vs Terraform Pulumi and Terraform  - Infrastructure as Code tools Terraform uses its own declarative language, HCL HCL = HashiCorp Configuration Language https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform Pulumi keeps the engine declarative but lets you write infrastructure in general-purpose languages like TypeScript, Python, or Go , it feel like a normal software project with functions, classes, and tests - https://www.pulumi.com Terraform remain industry standard Pulumi appeals more to developer teams # Terraform provider "aws" { region = "us-east-1" } resource "aws_s3_bucket" "mybucket" { bucket = "my-example-bucket" } resource "aws_s3_bucket_object" "index_html" { bucket = aws_s3_bucket.mybucket.id key    = "index.html" source = "./files/index.html" } # Pulumi import pulumi import pulumi_aws as aws bucket = aws.s3.Bucket("mybucket", bucket="my-example-bucket") index_html = aws.s3.BucketObject("indexHtml", bucket=bucket.id, key="index.html", source="./files/index.html") You can use AI agent (Claude Code) to create infra code. Example: Create a minimal Pulumi Python project for AWS. Requirements: - Use Python and the pulumi_aws package. - Create one private S3 bucket. - Enable versioning on the bucket. - Add tags: Project=demo and ManagedBy=Pulumi. - Export the bucket name and ARN. - Keep the code short and beginner-friendly. - Put the main code in __main__.py. - Also show the commands to initialize and run the project: - pulumi new aws-python - pulumi up Please output: 1. The full __main__.py file 2. A one-paragraph explanation of what the code does 3. The exact terminal commands to run it Do not add IAM policies, public access, website hosting, or extra resources unless I ask. Use the smallest working example. Claude Code uses the prompt above to generate files such as __main__.py, Pulumi.yaml, and often requirements.txt; then you run pulumi up command in that project directory.
